subject.title: [Feature]: Show session and requester context in macOS exec approval popup

question: What requester identity may the macOS exec approval dialog disclose, and how must session, channel, sender, account, and thread identifiers be shortened or redacted?
rationale: The existing session key can improve approval attribution, but it may embed private transport identifiers; richer requester fields expand that disclosure boundary and cannot be selected safely from source mechanics alone.

options.title: Redacted Session First
options.body: Show a human-readable, shortened session identity now and defer additional requester fields until their trust and redaction contracts are defined.

options.title: Structured Requester Context
options.body: Add typed channel, sender, destination, and thread fields with explicit provenance, sanitization, length limits, and upgrade tests in one broader change.

options.title: Keep Current Disclosure
options.body: Leave the native dialog unchanged and rely on command, agent, host, and external session surfaces for attribution.

recommendation.title: Redacted Session First
recommendation.body: Show a human-readable, shortened session identity now and defer additional requester fields until their trust and redaction contracts are defined.

likelyOwner.reason: This person supplied the prior item-specific review and is the strongest available owner for resolving the native UX and disclosure boundary.
